assumptions: The model name is resolved as the standard one-flavour massive U(1) Schwinger model with the displayed Lagrangian.
No gauge fixing, boundary condition, regulator, field truncation, or simulation algorithm is fixed at the continuum-theory stage.
No discrete-symmetry eigenvalue is inferred for either external state.

definitions.canonical_expression: L = -(1/4) F_{mu nu} F^{mu nu} + bar(psi) (i gamma^mu D_mu - m) psi; D_mu = partial_mu + i g A_mu; F_{mu nu} = partial_mu A_nu - partial_nu A_mu
H = integral_Sigma dx [ (1/2) E^2 + psi^dagger (-i alpha partial_1 + g alpha A_1 + m beta) psi + A_0 (g psi^dagger psi - partial_1 E) ]; E = F_01; alpha = gamma^0 gamma^1; beta = gamma^0
O(z1,z2) = bar(psi)(X(z1)) gamma^- W(X(z1),X(z2)) psi(X(z2)); X(z)^mu = a z n^mu; n=(1,1); gamma^- = gamma^0-gamma^1; z1 in [-2,-1,0,1,2]; z2 in [0]
W(x,y) = path_ordered_exp[-i g integral_y^x A_mu(xi) dxi^mu], oriented from the psi insertion y to the bar(psi) insertion x along the supplied straight lattice path

downstream_compatibility_requirements: Preserve number of lattice site: L = 5.
Use temporal spacing equal to spatial spacing.
Support z1 = [-2,-1,0,1,2] and z2 = [0] without dropping samples.
Preserve the ordered bar(psi)-Wilson-line-psi observable and the supplied straight lattice path.
Return both real and imaginary components.
Do not subtract vacuum energy from the simulated Hamiltonian.

model.gauge_structure: local U(1) gauge theory with one Dirac fermion flavour
model.name: Schwinger model

observable_specification.gauge_invariance: gauge invariant because the oriented Wilson line cancels the endpoint transformations of bar(psi)(X_1) and psi(X_2)
observable_specification.name: user_observable

resolved_conventions.gauge_transformation: psi->exp(-i g lambda)psi; bar(psi)->bar(psi)exp(i g lambda); A_mu->A_mu+partial_mu lambda

symmetries.operator_expression: G[lambda] = integral_Sigma dx lambda(x) [partial_1 E(x) - g psi^dagger(x) psi(x)]
P^nu = integral_Sigma dx T^{0 nu}; H=P^0
M^{01} = integral_Sigma dx [x^0 T^{01} - x^1 T^{00}]

symmetries.field_action: psi -> C bar(psi)^T; A_mu -> -A_mu; C gamma^{mu T} C^{-1} = -gamma^mu
psi(t,x) -> gamma^0 psi(t,-x); A_0(t,x) -> A_0(t,-x); A_1(t,x) -> -A_1(t,-x)
symmetries.relevance_note: The sampled spatial coordinate values occur in x to -x pairs, but P alone need not map the correlated points (z,z) into the sampled null line, and it exchanges gamma^- with gamma^+.

symmetries.field_action: psi(t,x) -> gamma^0 psi(-t,x); A_0(t,x) -> A_0(-t,x); A_1(t,x) -> -A_1(-t,x), with complex conjugation
symmetries.relevance_note: The sampled temporal coordinate values occur in t to -t pairs, but T alone need not map the correlated points (z,z) into the sampled null line, and it exchanges gamma^- with gamma^+.
PT maps X(z)=a z(1,1) to X(-z), which is sampled. No matrix-element identity is inferred because external-state PT eigenvalues were not supplied.
